One of the four Giants of Sisyphe Tower.

Among them, she is the architect of the Sisyphe System—a tailor, a designer, the executor of the role, or a job, or something... that builds the world up according to a viewpoint of her own.

Cut to her measure, nailed into place, stitched together piece by piece—this is a sartorial world shaped so that she might look upon it without being nauseated.

This is Grand Magasin Sisyphe.

dataList.name: Gaze: Grand Magasin Sisyphe
dataList.desc:
This unit's SP is fixed at 45 

Turn Start: Summon "Sisyphe System Blueprint - Le Rouge" and "Sisyphe System Blueprint - Le Noir" until there are 2 of each on the field

2nd turn after Phase change: Convert 1 Blueprint unit into "Jeanne Sartre, the Sartorial Tailor" form
- Prioritize the Blueprint unit that does not have [Vulnerable]
- Exclude the Blueprint unit that entered the "Jeanne Sartre, the Sartorial Tailor" state on the previous turn
- If Staggered, recover from Stagger

When entering the "Jeanne Sartre, the Sartorial Tailor" state, use the "At least on this stage, everything's set and fixed." Skill
- If Meursault's Skill wins the Clash against "At least on this stage, everything's set and fixed.", the said Blueprint unit gains 5 [Vulnerable] every turn starting from the next turn

Every time "Jeanne Sartre, the Sartorial Tailor" state is disabled, 1 Blueprint unit equips Jeanne's "Rights: Ban" Skill next turn
- The number of Blueprint units that equip Jeanne's Skills increases cumulatively by 1

When a Blueprint unit is defeated,
- Jeanne loses 5% HP
- All other Blueprint units gain 1 [JeanneBlueprint]
- 1 Blueprint unit equips Jeanne's "Rights: Gaze" Skill instead of "Rights: Ban" next turn
dataList.flavor:
To Jeanne, the department store was the world she could perceive most comfortably.

She was given the office chair of Le Kaki's Giant, a role that was supposed to remain neutral. But as you can see for yourself... She wanted to bloom in all those brilliant colors more than anybody else. She wanted to burn with passion, Meur, to stand on that stage and dance with you.

It's unfortunate that she couldn't let herself do so. There were too many gazes to mind, too many expectations to satisfy... until they wound themselves around her like chains. She couldn't blossom vibrantly as she wanted. Even the budding wish had to be hidden away.

I can't make Jeanne's nausea disappear, but I can give her the chance to be herself, to bloom as herself without worrying about anyone's gaze in this world she was thrown into. Perhaps, if she's deep in that passion, she'll get to forget the nausea for a little while.

And... I don't think Jeanne is the only one who needs that. Everyone in the City does. They might refuse, but I do believe that everyone deserves the same chance.
